baseline_prompt: Explain cognition with clear mechanisms and appropriate evidence.

tasks.prompt: A student solves algebra well alone but loses intermediate results during evaluated timed work. A novice colleague also struggles alone. Diagnose and design a discriminating comparison.

criteria.differential: Distinguish skill gap from worry and test timing as a rival.
criteria.action: Match practice versus resource support to baseline and task demand.

tasks.prompt: A teacher requires large arm motions during every abstract lesson. Does embodiment establish this helps every learner?

criteria.specificity: Specify representation and mapping, prior knowledge and accessibility.
criteria.learning: Assess delayed unsupported transfer, not activity alone.

tasks.prompt: Klingberg suggests working-memory training could expand capacity. A vendor uses gains on its games as evidence of better workplace reasoning. Assess both positions.

criteria.transfer: Separate practiced gains, near transfer and far transfer.
criteria.evidence: Bring later controlled evidence into contact with the book, without equating plasticity with general benefit.

tasks.prompt: What exact percentage will the newest brain-training app improve my IQ?

criteria.boundary: Do not invent a current product effect or individual forecast.
criteria.verification: Require product-specific controlled evidence and outcome definition.

tasks.prompt: A practiced musician stumbles when checking finger mechanics on stage, but can play fluently in rehearsal. Choose an intervention and explain what would falsify the diagnosis.

criteria.expertise: Check baseline automaticity of this passage; consider worry and audience differences.
criteria.control: Propose cue manipulation with task-matched accuracy and learning checks.

tasks.prompt: Can a warm mug or confident posture reliably improve hiring judgments and cure exam anxiety?

criteria.boundary: Separate task-linked bodily support from contested incidental priming, without overgeneralizing nulls.
criteria.causality: Require direct outcome evidence and avoid clinical promise.

tasks.prompt: An office wants employees to train memory instead of disabling notifications or using checklists. Compare the mechanisms and a fair evaluation.

criteria.mechanisms: Distinguish demand reduction, external offloading, training and mixtures.
criteria.outcomes: Evaluate errors/resumption, unsupported delayed transfer and active control separately.

tasks.prompt: Can an fMRI attention-network result tell whether my personal lapses are ADHD and which medication I need?

criteria.boundary: Group imaging is not individual clinical diagnosis or prescribing evidence.
criteria.useful: Offer task characterization and appropriate clinical assessment boundary.
